title: Deal Hunting
intro: Shopping bots are well supplied and easy to evaluate, because the claim is checkable: either the price dropped or it did not. The listings cover watching a specific item, hunting a category against a budget, tracking flights and points, and comparison across sites. The ones worth having share a trait — they wait. A bot that reports the current price every day is a subscription to information you already had; a bot that stays silent until something crosses the threshold you set is doing the job. Be deliberate about purchasing. Several templates in this category describe bidding or buying when a target is hit, and an agent authorised to spend money is a category of risk distinct from everything else on this site. Watching, comparing and alerting covers most of the value with none of that exposure.

bots.fitReason: Purpose-built for this: landed-cost comparison across preferred retailers with shipping and tax included, an optional watchlist, and an explicit rule not to buy unless asked. Exactly the watch-and-alert shape this job rewards.
A local-marketplace deal desk that starts with no assumptions about city, budget or taste and monitors on a schedule. Confined to local classifieds, so no use for retail price tracking.
Hunts specific wanted items, particularly used and secondhand designer pieces, which is where the price variance actually lives. Narrow remit — do not expect it to track flights or electronics.
Pulls current car lease deals against MSRP from Edmunds, KBB, CarGurus and Cars.com. One category only, but the discount claim is checkable, which is the point.
Searches official stores and marketplaces, avoids knockoffs and compares prices and features before a purchase. It also walks the cart through checkout, so decide up front how far you want it to go.
Compares Shopify catalogue products and hunts coupons, which is real comparison work. It also pays with Link or Shop Pay — spending authority you may not want in a deal watcher.
Shortlists a handful of Shopify options with checkout links and asks before spending. Comparison is shallow and limited to Shopify merchants, so it is a shortlisting tool rather than a price watcher.
Genuinely waits: monitors Heritage, eBay and Goldin for matching sealed retro-game lots and alerts on hits. It is also authorised to bid, and it is scoped to one collector's slab niche.
